texts: mixed: the collecting, the keepers and lanterns of the Harbor Row, the threads with their silken/thread decomposition, the source and dawn all come through, and "together" earns its place by suppressing the per-keeper distribution rule. The shortfall is "day 301 of Year 1": the translator's day term is the day-within-a-month slot and it has no day-of-year term, so the number lands in a slot that means something else. No rewrite preserves a day-of-year count, so leave it unless your calendar can name a month — "On the thirteenth day of Thawmonth in Year 1, the keepers of the Harbor Row together collected the silken threads from the lanterns of the Harbor Row at dawn." parses fully.
good. the carrying reuses the same keepers and threads, Cauldron Hall is typed and named as the destination, and a fireable per-keeper rule sits beside the group event.
good. Hesper, the boiling, the threads as what is changed and sea-water as where it happens all parse, with sea-water decomposed to water.

good. "Mire-essence" gets its own individual here rather than a bare class symbol, which is what keeps the later "the mire-essence" mentions on one symbol; "by evening" is recorded as a deadline bound rather than an exact time, which is right.
good. the four clay vessels parse as a counted group, the essence is the same one that formed, and storing leaves it unchanged so it is filed as moved rather than altered.

good. the drawing reuses the keepers and the same essence, keeps sundown, and adds a fireable per-keeper rule; "the stored" gets no atom of its own, but the coreference to the storing event already pins which essence is meant.
good. the thirty feathers parse as a counted subset of the fallen-feather set, with "fallen" handed to each member by a fireable rule, and the base of the cliff and the morning both come through.
good. the same thirty feathers are added, and the feather bin is typed and decomposed to bin as the destination.
good. bare "feathers" correctly mints a new group taken from the same bin — nothing claims they are the same thirty, which matches what the sentence says.
good. the grinding reuses those feathers and files them as changed by it, which is right.
good. the agentless passive parses as a lighting of the named, typed Stilllight Lantern with no invented lighter.
good. the scattering reuses the ground feathers, keeps "around the Stilllight Lantern" as its own relation rather than forcing it into a location, and keeps sundown.

good. the warding parses with the feathers as what does it, the lantern as what is warded, and "against wraiths" kept as its own relation on the wraith kind; unlike sentences 2 and 6 it stays collective with no per-feather rule, which reads as the scattered feathers warding as one.

mixed: the non-occurrence is stored as a strength-zero rule over the whole wraith kind, so it reads closer to "no wraith ever approaches this lantern at night" than to "none did on this one night" — the only limit on it is the bare day-part "night", because "that night" carried no day with it. Pin the night so the denial is bounded to it: "On the night of day 301 of Year 1, no wraith approached the Stilllight Lantern." (the day-of-year caveat from sentence 1 still applies).
